The company hiked its full-year forecast for the third straight quarter. Matteo Della Torre | Nurphoto | Getty Images Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its full-year outlook for the third straight quarter, despite lackluster demand in its home market. For the full year, Coke now expects comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from its prior forecast of an increase in the range of 9% to 10%. The beverage giant also anticipates that its organic revenue will climb at least 5%, a slight increase from its previous outlook of approximately 5% growth. Shares of the company rose about 1% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting: Earnings per share: 91 cents adjusted vs. 88 cents expected Revenue: $13.4 billion vs. $12.92 billion expected Coke reported third-quarter net income attributable to shareholders of $4.01 billion, or 93 cents per share, up from $3.7 billion, or 86 cents per share, a year earlier. Excluding transaction gains and other items, Coke earned 91 cents per share. Net sales rose 7% to $13.4 billion. Coke's organic revenue, which strips out acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency, also rose 7% in the quarter. For the second straight quarter, the company's unit case volume increased 5%, helped by higher demand outside of North America. Coke's home market reported flat volume. However, the company's North American business would have reported volume growth if not for the timing of the Fourth of July holiday and the months-long shortage of Topo Chico, a sparkling water brand Coke owns, CFO John Murphy told CNBC. "The underlying momentum remains quite strong," he said. "Consumer sentiment is largely unchanged in the sense that, wherever you are on the income scale, you're looking for value, and I think our system here has done a good job interpreting that." In recent quarters, Coke executives have said North American shoppers are under pressure, stretched thin by inflation and economic uncertainty. But the beverage giant has also said consumers are still buying its drinks, from premium brands like Fairlife to its namesake soda. Globally, Coke's sparkling soft drinks business saw volume increase 5% during the quarter, lifted by growth of Coke, Coke Zero Sugar and Diet Coke. Diet Coke is having a "resurgence," Murphy said. Gen Z consumers in the U.S. have nicknamed it a "fridge cigarette," while consumers in India threw Diet Coke parties as shortages tied to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran have made the drink scarce. "It's a brand that's almost reinventing itself with the next generation of consumers," he said. Coke has also gained market share as rival PepsiCo sees its soda business struggle, according to Murphy. Still, some of Coke's soda brands, like Sprite, have "some work to do." Coke's water, sports, coffee and tea division also saw volume climb by 5%. Increased demand for its water, which includes its premium Smartwater brand, fueled the growth. Demand for its tea and coffee was flat, while sports drinks declined. The company's juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages business reported flat volume, despite growth in brands like Fairlife and Minute Maid. headlines.article_text: Boeing (BA) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose. The company beat revenue expectations but posted a bigger loss per share than expected. Boeing executives will host an earnings conference call at 10:30 a.m. ET. In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:39 01:39 Boeing narrows third-quarter loss as defense sales rise, but focus remains on 737 Max production Squawk Box Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose, but CEO Kelly Ortberg told staff that the manufacturer has "more work to do." Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts are expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG: Loss per share: 34 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 21 cents expected Revenue: $24.19 billion expected vs $23.84 billion expected. For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company reported a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program. Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company's defense unit revenue rose 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion. Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier. Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said. The plane manufacturer's executives are set to update investors on how quickly it can increase aircraft production in the coming months when it holds a quarterly earnings call on Tuesday at 10:30 a.m. ET. Boeing has been producing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month, but is aiming for more. CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors last month that production is taking "a little bit longer" than expected to stabilize, and the company expects to increase its output of the planes next year. "Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality." Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it. But the manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet. And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: PYPL, GLW, UPS, KO Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making headlines before the bell: PayPal — Shares slipped 1% after the digital payments platform reported a revenue miss in its third-quarter report. The company reported revenue of $8.58 billion, compared to an LSEG estimate of $8.71 billion. Earnings, however, beat estimates and PayPal raised its full-year profit forecast. Corning — The materials science stock popped nearly 3% on third-quarter results that exceeded expectations. Corning reported earnings of 91 cents per share, excluding items, on revenue of $5.08 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected per-share earnings of 88 cents on revenues of $5.02 billion. UPS — The package delivery company gained 1.6% after it reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance. UPS projects full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion. Coca-Cola — Shares of the beverage giant gained 0.3% after Coca-Cola said it raised its full-year outlook for a third straight quarter, in spite of lackluster demand in its home market. Coke expects comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from its prior forecast of an increase in the range of 9% to 10%. It also anticipates that its organic revenue will climb at least 5%, a slight increase from its previous outlook of approximately 5% growth. Nvidia , Meta Platforms — Nvidia said it will invest $3 billion in Meta after the social media and artificial intelligence giant announced plans to raise up to $95 billion to support its investments in AI infrastructure. Shares of Nvidia gained 0.7%, while Meta Platforms dipped 0.3%. Amkor Technology — Shares of the semiconductor packaging and testing company rose more than 3.5% despite the company missing analysts' third-quarter earnings and revenue expectations. Amkor reported earnings of 76 cents per share and revenue of $1.99 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected earnings of 78 cents per share and $2.04 billion in revenue. Amkor also reduced its capital expenditure outlook to around $2.5 billion for the fiscal year, versus prior guidance of between $2.5 billion and $3 billion. Royal Caribbean — Shares advanced 4.4% after the company reported third-quarter earnings that beat analyst expectations. The cruise line operator earned $6.57 per share, excluding certain items, topping a FactSet forecast of $6.38 per share. The company also raised its full-year earnings guidance for 2026. Boeing — The aerospace company was slightly higher by 0.5% after it reported mixed financials for the third-quarter . While it posted a loss that was wider than expected, revenue came in above an LSEG consensus. Whirlpool — The home appliance company tumbled 7% after reporting disappointing earnings and guidance. Whirlpool lost an adjusted 21 cents per share on revenue of $3.68 billion for its third quarter. Analysts were expecting adjusted earnings of 80 cents per share on revenue of $3.92 billion, per LSEG. The company also cut its full-year revenue guidance to $14.5 billion from $15 billion. It expects a full-year loss of $1.30 per share, versus the consensus estimate of a $1.55 per share profit. JetBlue Airways — The air carrier climbed more than 11% after JetBlue said it expects further margin expansion in the fourth quarter even as fuel prices are anticipated to be 85% higher than a year earlier. JetBlue reported an adjusted loss of 60 cents a share in the third quarter, compared to the 55-cent loss analysts polled by LSEG had sought. Revenue narrowly missed expectations, as well. Celestica — The supply chain management company surged nearly 15% after Celestica raised its full-year guidance. It anticipates adjusted earnings of $11.55 per share, up from its earlier call for $11.30 per share and beating the FactSet consensus forecast for $11.16. Cadence Design Systems — The electronic systems design company rose 1.8% after third-quarter results passed estimates and raised its full-year revenue growth outlook. Cadence Design earned $2.11 per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $1.63 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG sought $2.05 per share and $1.61 billion. — CNBC's Ananya Chetia, Michelle Fox, Davis Giangiulio, Fred Imbert, Paulina Likos, Amelia Lucas, Darla Mercado, Laya Neelakandan and Kai Nicol-Schwarz contributed reporting

headlines.article_text: GM will switch to Nasdaq from the NYSE on Nov. 17 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points General Motors plans to transfer its common-stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq, with trading expected to begin Nov. 17. The automaker expects to keep its “GM” ticker symbol, and the company says shareholders do not need to take action because of the transfer. The transfer would make GM eligible for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index, while aligning the listing with GM’s technology-driven strategy. In this article GM NDAQ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:06 01:06 GM to move from NYSE to Nasdaq Squawk Box DETROIT — General Motors plans to transfer shares of its common stock from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq as the automaker attempts to position itself more as a technology-focused company. The Detroit automaker said Tuesday that it expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq -listed company on Nov. 17. Its ticker symbol is expected to remain "GM," the company said. "GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," GM CFO Paul Jacobson said in a release. "We're grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy." GM noted the move will provide eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index . Current shareholders do not need to take any action with respect to the transfer, the company said. The switch marks a notable loss for the NYSE, as GM first listed on the exchange in 1911. The Detroit automaker also relisted on the stock exchange in 2010 following a government-backed bankruptcy. General Motors vs. Ford Motor stock GM follows other companies such as Walmart , DoorDash and Palantir Technologies that have transferred from the more traditional NYSE to the historically technology focused Nasdaq in recent years. Hilton Worldwide Holdings last week also announced plans to move trading from the NYSE to Nasdaq. The key drivers for a listing transfer differ from company to company, but the Nasdaq in 2024 said common reasons include "index inclusion opportunities, cost effective fee structure, brand visibility partnership, access to Nasdaq's event space, and Nasdaq's suite of investor relations and ESG products." GM's decision comes a week after the automaker held a technology-focused event where executives laid out the company's roadmap for artificial intelligence and self-driving vehicle technologies. Shares of GM, which has been aggressively buying back stock , have more than doubled since 2024. GM's stock closed Monday at $76.31 per share. The company's market cap is roughly $64.4 billion.
